findings.location: content.body.titleUk: "Прикметники на -e та на приголосну: одна форма для обох родів"; content.body.ruleUk: "Прикметники на -e і більшість прикметників на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів".
findings.description: The title presents consonant-ending adjectives as universally invariant in gender. The rule qualifies consonant endings but still generalizes across all -e endings. Counterexamples include trabajador/trabajadora and regordete/regordeta. Nationality adjectives are not the only consonant-ending group with gender variation.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly scope the title and rule to the listed invariant adjectives, or qualify both ending groups. Present nationality adjectives as one example of exceptions.

items.reviewerAnswer: Grande, verde, azul, fácil and joven have the same masculine and feminine forms, while agreeing in number.
items.notes: All the listed example forms are correct.
sources: Course contract, rule 8: Spanish correctness.
RAE/ASALE, Diccionario de la lengua española, entries «trabajador, ra», «regordete, ta» and «español, la» (from memory).

findings.location: content.body.steps[1].blocks[0].text: "Прикметники на -e і більшість прикметників на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів"; content.body.steps[8].blocks[0].items[1]: "Прикметник на -e чи приголосну: одна форма для обох родів, у множині -s або -es."
findings.description: The summary removes the qualification on consonant endings and states a false universal rule. The explanation also treats every -e adjective as gender-invariant. Español/española, trabajador/trabajadora and regordete/regordeta demonstrate the limits of these generalizations.
findings.suggestion: Scope both passages to the adjectives introduced here, or qualify both ending groups. Preserve that qualification in the summary.

items.reviewerAnswer: The lesson should teach gender and number agreement, selected gender-invariant adjectives, usual postnominal position, invariant muy and short-description comprehension.
items.notes: The examples, use of muy and terminology «знак наголосу» are correct.
sources: Course contract, rule 8: Spanish correctness.
RAE/ASALE, Diccionario de la lengua española, entries «español, la», «trabajador, ra» and «regordete, ta» (from memory).

findings.description: The prompt fixes definiteness but does not establish a neutral restrictive description rather than an expressive description. Those readings permit different adjective positions, so the incorrect outcome depends on an unstated register or interpretation.
findings.suggestion: Specify that the learner must use the usual neutral postnominal order, or leave the expressive prenominal alternative unresolved.

items.reviewerAnswer: las flores blancas. Las blancas flores is also possible in an expressive, nonrestrictive description.
sources: Verdict definition: uncertain when acceptability depends on unspecified context or register.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 13, adjective position and restrictive versus nonrestrictive interpretation (from memory).

findings.description: A neutral classified listing supports the expected order, while expressive advertising can license marked prenominal color adjectives. The prompt identifies an advertisement but does not specify which register is intended.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly request a neutral listing with the color adjective after the noun, or leave the marked alternative unresolved.

items.reviewerAnswer: una moto roja for an ordinary sales listing. Una roja moto would require a stylized, expressive advertising register.
items.notes: The agreement and the use of feminine moto are correct.
sources: Verdict definition: uncertain when acceptability depends on unspecified register.

findings.location: task.prompt[0].text: "Пам’ятай: прикметники на -e і на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів; змінюється тільки число."; task.hints[0].blocks[0].text: "Прикметники на -e і на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів".
findings.description: Both passages teach gender invariance as a universal property of these endings. Consonant-ending adjectives such as español and trabajador have feminine forms; even -e has exceptions such as regordete/regordeta.
findings.suggestion: State that the listed adjectives, including grande and azul, do not vary by gender, or qualify both ending groups.

items.reviewerAnswer: una casa grande; the adjective form is grande.
items.notes: The answer key itself is correct.
sources: Course contract, rule 8: Spanish correctness.

findings.location: task.prompt[0].text: "Пам’ятай: прикметники на -e і на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів; змінюється тільки число."; task.hints[0].blocks[0].text: "Прикметники на -e і на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів".
findings.description: The reminder and hint falsely generalize gender invariance to all adjectives with these endings. Español/española and trabajador/trabajadora contradict the consonant rule; regordete/regordeta contradicts the unrestricted -e rule.
findings.suggestion: Limit the rule to the invariant adjectives introduced here. Keep the correct explanation azul → azules.

items.reviewerAnswer: unos libros azules; the adjective form is azules.

findings.location: task.hints[0].blocks[0].text: "Прикметники на -e і на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів".
findings.description: The general hint falsely says that all adjectives ending in -e or a consonant are gender-invariant. Español/española, trabajador/trabajadora and regordete/regordeta show otherwise.
findings.suggestion: Scope the rule to the invariant adjectives introduced here, and state specifically that joven has plural jóvenes for both genders.

items.reviewerAnswer: unas chicas jóvenes; jóvenes alone also supplies the corrected adjective.
items.notes: The required written accent in jóvenes is correctly identified.

findings.location: task.hints[0].blocks[0].text: "Прикметники на -e і на приголосну мають одну форму для обох родів"; task.errors[1].feedbackUk: "Перед іменником grande скорочується до gran і означає «чудовий, величний»; для «великий» кажемо un hotel grande."
findings.description: The hint falsely universalizes gender invariance. The feedback also presents gran as necessarily evaluative and excludes its physical-size meaning. Prenominal gran is not restricted to 'excellent' or 'magnificent'.
findings.suggestion: Scope the invariance rule to the selected adjectives. Explain that gran often has an evaluative meaning but can also describe size; retain unresolved treatment unless the prompt fixes the intended reading.

items.reviewerAnswer: un hotel grande for physical size. Un gran hotel can express excellence and can also refer to size, depending on context.

findings.description: The reminder says that adjectives usually follow nouns, but the instruction only asks for a phrase assembled from the words. It does not explicitly require the usual neutral order. The prenominal alternative's acceptability therefore depends on an unspecified expressive versus neutral register.
findings.suggestion: Ask explicitly for the usual neutral order or instruct the learner to put the adjective after the noun. Otherwise leave the expressive alternative unresolved.

items.reviewerAnswer: una casa blanca is the usual neutral order; una blanca casa is possible in expressive language.
sources: Verdict definition: uncertain when acceptability depends on unspecified register.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, chapter 13, adjective position and expressive prenominal uses (from memory).

findings.description: The task asks the learner to assemble a phrase without explicitly restricting its register or requiring postnominal order. The reminder establishes a usual pattern, not an absolute prohibition on expressive prenominal color adjectives.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly request the usual neutral order or require the adjective after the noun. Otherwise leave the marked alternative unresolved.

items.reviewerAnswer: un coche rojo is the usual neutral order; un rojo coche is possible in marked expressive language.
